attempted_claim: Let Q_n=[-1/2,1/2]^n, let 1≤k≤n−1, and let G_{n,k} be the Grassmannian of k-dimensional linear subspaces of R^n. Vaaler’s theorem gives vol_k(Q_n∩H)≥1 for every H∈G_{n,k}, with equality at coordinate subspaces. Determine the optimal universal stability modulus Φ(ε) such that, for every n,k and H∈G_{n,k}, vol_k(Q_n∩H)≤1+ε implies min_{I⊂[n], |I|=k} ||P_H−P_{span{e_i:i∈I}}||_{HS}≤Φ(ε), and prove matching lower examples showing the optimal order of Φ(ε) as ε→0.
decisive_failure: The k=1 exact sqrt(eps) computation and local graph-subspace linearization were verified numerically but are routine exercises, not original theorems; global uniformity over all n,k with matching extremal families remains unproved and would require a dimension-free reverse Brascamp-Lieb stability theory with degenerate data plus a full equality characterization.
